Goal: secure a qualified lease in 21 days or less.

An operating goal, not a guarantee. Move-in timing and screening still matter.

Compete on value from day one.

The most relevant completed four-bedroom leases both closed at $2,850. One took 20 days; the other took 74 days. Meanwhile, two directly competing four-bedroom homes remain offered at $2,850.

A $2,795 launch places this newer, nearly 2,000-square-foot home $55 below those asking prices. That modest difference supports the priority: finding a qualified resident promptly rather than spending the opening weeks testing an unsupported premium.

The market determines the achievable rent. Our job is to position the home well, monitor response and adjust promptly when the evidence calls for it.

Why timing matters

About 23 extra vacant days can consume nearly a year’s rent increase.

Suppose we compare $2,795 with a higher target of $2,995. The extra $200 per month is worth $2,400 over twelve full months. But 23 additional vacant days at the higher rate represent approximately $2,296 in foregone gross rent—almost the entire increase.

Same 360-day comparison windowGross rent
$2,795, beginning at the baseline start date$33,540
$2,995, beginning 23 days later$33,644
$2,995, beginning 25 days later$33,444

In this example, the advantage disappears after approximately 24 extra vacant days. At 25 days, the higher rent produces about $96 less gross income over the same window. Pricing well at launch helps avoid that trade-off.

Illustration uses 30-day months, no concessions or expenses, and an identical 360-day measurement period. The break-even point varies with the rent difference; 23 days is not a universal rule. These are additional vacant days beyond the earlier start date, not the total marketing period. $2,995 is a mathematical example, not the recommended asking rent.

A clear plan after launch

The first 21 days

Day 1 · LaunchBegin at $2,795 when vacant, show-ready and available for flexible tours. Use strong photography and clearly state included services.
Day 5 · Read the responseReview qualified inquiries, tours, applications and repeated feedback. Verify that listings and showing access are working properly.
Days 10–14 · ActIf interest is weak, address presentation or access issues immediately. If price is the obstacle, recommend a move to $2,750 rather than wait until day 21.
By day 21 · Secure a leaseAim for a fully screened, qualified resident and a dependable lease-start date. If unmet, reassess against the newest competition and completed leases.

We cannot predict an exact leasing date. We can make an evidence-based recommendation, listen to the market and respond quickly. A signed lease with a distant start date does not end vacancy; both the rent and the start date matter.

Recommended direction

Launch at $2,795 per month, present the home at its best and give qualified renters a compelling reason to choose it over the other available four-bedroom townhomes. The evidence supports competing near the $2,850 leased benchmark, while the 21-day objective favors a modest advantage rather than a higher opening test.
